effective_date_basis: (1) The date of the action from a dated record: a NARA St. Louis service record card or personnel folder, an agency report, or a later order's recital that dates the action itself. A recital may give only the waiver order's own date (EO 6179-A does), which is not the date of the action. (2) The interval (order date, R], with the record that supplies R: the Official Register (all employees in odd years 1901-1921, dated July 1 according to a secondary index; postal employees omitted after 1911; officials only from 1925), a later order naming the person in the authorized position, or an agency report. A match needs the full name, the office, and a position consistent with the order. Absence from the Register proves nothing; presence does not show which authority an appointment used, and does not show use of a retention or temporary-to-permanent order. (3) The interval (order date, reason date]: the revoking order's date (EO 3461: 1921-05-16), April 15, 1903, the death date, or the latest-possible-death bound, with 'use unknown' stated. The four Civil Service Commission annual reports read in full (FY1914, 1915, 1918 and 1922) print and count the orders but do not record whether or when an individual waiver was used; the other reports have not been read in full, so a report is a source for the action date only if a reading finds such a record.
ending_pattern: The order authorizes one personnel action for one named person (appointment, reinstatement, transfer, retention or examination without regard to a civil-service rule). Its permission is exhausted when the action is taken; the resulting appointment or status survives as an accrued effect of the action, not of the order, unless a later order revokes it. EO 6179-A (June 16, 1933) revoked, as 'appointments made by the President', ten waiver orders identified by their own dates; it ends any unused permission under them and any appointment made under them, and is not evidence that an appointment was made. Decide each order on the held evidence. (1) Exhausted on a date, when a dated record of the action is held. (2) Exhausted within the interval (order date, R], when a record shows the person in the authorized position at date R and not in it at the order date. (3) Not in force, use unknown, stated as the interval (order date, reason date], because a permission that was used ended earlier than the reason. Reasons: an express revocation, such as EO 3461 of May 16, 1921, which revoked 'all Executive orders and amendments to the civil service rules authorizing appointments, promotions, or removals without full compliance with the civil service laws and rules, because of war emergencies existing at the time' and lists the orders it revokes. A member in that list is expressly revoked; a member not in the list whose own text rests on the war emergency is covered only on a reading of the general clause (the list could instead be read as exhaustive), so state that reading as the basis. The held copy (jobs/csc-annual-reports/output/texts/EO_3461.txt) stops at item 27 of 45, so absence from the held list is not absence from the list. Other reasons: a 1900-1902 special rule that on reading names a person (EO 209 replaced the 1896 rules 'and the amendments thereof'); the named person's known death; or, as a bound only, the latest possible death. (4) Open, naming the records that would settle it. Whether the action happened is a separate question from when the permission ended: categories (3) and (4) keep the order open on use. The latest possible death is computed by subtracting a_min whole years from the order date and then adding 122 years 164 days (the longest authenticated life). a_min is 0 unless a quoted fact in the order or a held record fixes a minimum age, and then it is the lowest age that the quoted fact allows, not a typical age (for example, 'widow of' allows only the lowest lawful marriage age, not adulthood; dated earlier service fixes an age only if the earlier record states one); a position or professional title alone does not fix an adult age (the type includes a 'messenger boy', EO 2661). The bound counts only if it falls before the claim's legal cutoff date; state the a_min used and the smallest a_min at which the bound would fall before that cutoff. The later general rewrites of the Civil Service Rules (EO 7916 of 1938, EO 8743 of 1941, EO 9830 of 1947, EO 10577 of 1954) revoke only listed orders and schedules and list no one-person waiver, so they are not ends for these orders. EO 209 (1903) is a reason only for the special rules above, and a candidate only for other waivers issued before April 15, 1903.

exceptions_savings.assessment: The appointment or status conferred is an accrued effect that continues independently of the order (state transferred_or_accrued), unless a later order revokes it: EO 6179-A (June 16, 1933) revoked ten waiver orders as 'appointments made by the President', ending any unused permission and any appointment made under them, without showing that an appointment was made. The Act of March 27, 1922 and EO 9830 s.1.1(b) recognize competitive status granted by executive order, which supports the status surviving later rewrites of the Civil Service Rules. Later service rights flow from civil-service statutes, not from the order.

legal_effect: Research pattern only. A type rule never fills a judgment field, establishes an end, a date, a status or savings for any order, and never substitutes for reading the order's own text.
outlier_conditions: The order's own text (not only the WPA summary or APP title) does not match the type, or the held text is another order's.
The order does more than the type's single act (a second operative clause of another kind).
A later order or statute amends, extends, revokes or revives it before the candidate end.
The order states its own effective date, duration, condition or termination that differs from the pattern.

The order is not a one-person waiver on reading. Examples found so far (not a complete list): rule amendments (EO 60, 95, 123, 158, 164, 262, 332, 1582, 2121, 6043, 7137; type cs_rules_amendment); class orders and general authorities (EO 203, 222, about 30 others found in review; EO 715 on transfers and EO 983 on fourth-class postmasters, both revoked by EO 9830 effective May 1, 1947); land orders (EO 395, 3992); orders revoking other orders (EO 3461, 6179-A); and EO 2071 and 2284, found in review not to fit.
A 1900-1902 'special rule' for a position rather than a person (EO 130, 141-143, 154, 174, 185, unless on reading one names a person).

The order names several persons (EO 223, 226, 686, 1321, 3681): decide each person's permission separately; the order is spent only when every person's permission has ended, and its end is the latest of them.
The authority is continuing (for example 'may be appointed at any time').
The waiver is conditional (for example on a noncompetitive examination or probation) or limited to a stated position or period.
The order rests on the war emergency (1917-1921): check EO 3461's list and text as an express end.

The person is named again in a later order (serial waivers, retention or retirement orders, a later modification such as EO 7472 of EO 7140, or a revocation of the appointment such as EO 6179-A): read both; the later order may supply use evidence or an end.
The order converts a temporary employee to permanent status or retains an employee: presence in the position is not evidence of use.
The held text is printed in a Civil Service Commission annual report, so the report's commentary or neighbouring orders can bleed into the slice.

required_evidence: The order's own text naming the person, the action and the rule waived.

A dated record of the action, a record bounding it, or a stated reason the permission ended; otherwise the order stays open, naming the records that would settle it (the Official Register for the next listing date; the NARA St. Louis card).

A bounded later-law search for an order or statute naming this order or the person (revocation, including EO 3461's list; modification; confirmation; revocation of the appointment itself; or a later order showing the person in the position).

scope.note: Membership is a machine lead; each order is decided by an agent, row by row.
